proposals.before: He killed Luo at Xihai, appointed his son Yin General Who Spreads Might, and led fifty thousand men to oppose Lü Guang at Jiuquan.
proposals.after: He killed Luo at Xihai, appointed his son Yin General Who Spreads Might, and sent him with fifty thousand men to oppose Lü Guang at Jiuquan.
proposals.reason: The subject of 率眾五萬 is Liang Xi's son Yin, not Liang Xi; the current wording assigns the command to the wrong person.

proposals.before: Fu Yin met Lü Guang at Anmi and was routed.
proposals.after: Liang Yin met Lü Guang at Anmi and was routed.
proposals.reason: 胤 is Liang Xi's son Liang Yin from s0043; calling him Fu Yin gives him the wrong surname.

proposals.before: Suo Pan, administrator of Jianwei and Xijun, and Song Hao, administrator of Jiuquan who held the office of general who rouses might and supervised military affairs south of Hongchi Pool, together with others, were all killed by Lü Guang.
proposals.after: Suo Pan, General Who Establishes Might and administrator of Xijun, and Song Hao, administrator of Jiuquan who held the office of General Who Rouses Might and supervised military affairs south of Hongchi Pool, together with others, were all killed by Lü Guang.
proposals.reason: 建威 is Suo Pan's military title, not a commandery administered by him.

proposals.before: Suo Pan, who held Jianwei and the western commandery, Song Hao of Jiuquan—who served as general who rouses might and directed troops south of Hongchi—and others likewise fell to Lü Guang's blade.
proposals.after: Suo Pan, general who establishes might and administrator of Xijun, Song Hao of Jiuquan—who served as general who rouses might and directed troops south of Hongchi—and others likewise fell to Lü Guang's blade.
proposals.reason: The current wording obscures 建威 as a military office and 西郡太守 as the separate commandery appointment.

proposals.before: Xing sent the General Who Establishes the Lineage, Bai Wei of Linqing, leading seventeen hundred of his clansmen by night to strike Guang's army and inflicted a great defeat on them.
proposals.after: Xing sent Bai Weiping of Linqing, General Who Establishes the Standard, to lead seventeen hundred of his clansmen in a night attack on Guang's army, inflicting a great defeat on it.
proposals.reason: 臨清柏衛平 gives the full name Bai Weiping (柏衛平), and 建節將軍 is a military title; the current text truncates the name and mistranslates 節 as lineage.

proposals.before: Mao Xing dispatched Bai Wei of Linqing, general who establishes the lineage, with seventeen hundred kinsmen in a night attack that shattered Wang Guang's camp.
proposals.after: Mao Xing dispatched Bai Weiping of Linqing, general who establishes the standard, with seventeen hundred kinsmen in a night attack that shattered Wang Guang's camp.
proposals.reason: The source names 柏衛平, Bai Weiping, and 建節 is a military title involving the command standard, not lineage.

proposals.before: The Di of Fuhan were all harried by war and too worn to obey; they killed Xing, raised Wei Ping to Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Hezhou, and sent envoys to ask for orders.
proposals.after: The Di of Fuhan were all harried by war and too worn to obey; they killed Xing, raised Bai Weiping to Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Hezhou, and sent envoys to ask for orders.
proposals.reason: 衛平 is the given name of Bai Weiping (柏衛平), introduced in s0082, not a person surnamed Wei.

proposals.before: The Di clans of Fuhan, battered by constant fighting, could bear no more; they assassinated Mao Xing, proclaimed Wei Ping inspector of Hezhou with the titles bearer of the imperial tally and general who pacifies the west, and begged the court for confirmation.
proposals.after: The Di clans of Fuhan, battered by constant fighting, could bear no more; they assassinated Mao Xing, proclaimed Bai Weiping inspector of Hezhou with the titles bearer of the imperial tally and general who pacifies the west, and begged the court for confirmation.
proposals.reason: The full name supplied in s0082 is Bai Weiping (柏衛平).

proposals.before: The Di clans of Fuhan, because Wei Ping was old and could not accomplish great undertakings, debated deposing him, yet feared the strength of his lineage and for days could not decide.
proposals.after: The Di clans of Fuhan, because Bai Weiping was old and could not accomplish great undertakings, debated deposing him, yet feared the strength of his lineage and for days could not decide.
proposals.reason: 衛平 refers back to Bai Weiping (柏衛平), not a person surnamed Wei.

proposals.before: In Fuhan the Di elders agreed that Wei Ping was too aged to lead, but they hesitated to depose him because his clan was powerful, and the council dragged on without resolution.
proposals.after: In Fuhan the Di elders agreed that Bai Weiping was too aged to lead, but they hesitated to depose him because his clan was powerful, and the council dragged on without resolution.
proposals.reason: The full name supplied in s0082 is Bai Weiping (柏衛平).

proposals.before: Wei Ping is a spent old man—he should step aside for someone fit to rule. Fu Deng of Didao, though only a minor kinsman of the throne, has vision and courage; let us raise him up and march to the emperor's banner.
proposals.after: Bai Weiping is a spent old man—he should step aside for someone fit to rule. Fu Deng of Didao, though only a minor kinsman of the throne, has vision and courage; let us raise him up and march to the emperor's banner.
proposals.reason: The full name supplied in s0082 is Bai Weiping (柏衛平).

proposals.before: His father Chang, in Fu Jian's time, had been marshal to the grand commandant, administrator of Longdong, general who establishes the lineage, and was later killed by Fu Sheng.
proposals.after: His father Chang, in Fu Jian's time, had been marshal to the grand commandant, administrator of Longdong, General Who Establishes the Standard, and was later killed by Fu Sheng.
proposals.reason: 建節將軍 is a military title involving the command standard; 'establishes the lineage' mistranslates 節.

proposals.before: His father Fu Chang had served as marshal to the grand commandant, governor of Longdong, and general who establishes the lineage under Fu Jian, until Fu Sheng put him to death.
proposals.after: His father Fu Chang had served as marshal to the grand commandant, governor of Longdong, and general who establishes the standard under Fu Jian, until Fu Sheng put him to death.
proposals.reason: 建節將軍 is a military title involving the command standard, not lineage.

proposals.before: Once Deng had replaced Wei Ping, he then held sole command of campaigns.
proposals.after: Once Deng had replaced Bai Weiping, he then held sole command of campaigns.
proposals.reason: 衛平 refers to Bai Weiping (柏衛平), introduced in s0082.

proposals.before: After Fu Deng succeeded Wei Ping he alone led the armies.
proposals.after: After Fu Deng succeeded Bai Weiping he alone led the armies.
proposals.reason: The full name supplied in s0082 is Bai Weiping (柏衛平).

proposals.before: The bandit enemies are not yet pacified; you cannot among the imperial clan make yourselves mutual foes—I pray the Great King follow in the tracks of Guangwu's yielding to the Duke of Geng, and after beheading the two bandits, slowly plan further."
proposals.after: The bandit enemies are not yet pacified; you cannot make yourselves mutual foes within the imperial clan. I pray the Great King follow Guangwu's example of deferring to the Gengshi Emperor, and after beheading the two bandits, slowly plan further."
proposals.reason: 聖公 is the Gengshi Emperor, Liu Xuan, not a 'Duke of Geng.'

proposals.before: The rebels still hold the field—you must not turn kinsman against kinsman. Follow Guangwu's example with the Geng emperor: destroy the two usurpers first, then debate the succession."
proposals.after: The rebels still hold the field—you must not turn kinsman against kinsman. Follow Guangwu's example in deferring to the Gengshi Emperor: destroy the two usurpers first, then debate the succession."
proposals.reason: 聖公 is the established title of the Gengshi Emperor, not 'the Geng emperor.'

proposals.before: My elder brother Xiang crossed north from the south of Shan, borrowing a road to seek the west; the fox dies with its head toward its mound—he wished briefly to see his homeland.
proposals.after: My elder brother Xiang crossed northward from Shan, borrowing a road to seek the west; the fox dies with its head toward its mound—he wished briefly to see his homeland.
proposals.reason: 從陝北渡 means that he crossed northward from Shan; the source does not say 'from the south of Shan.'

proposals.before: My brother Xiang crossed from south of Shan bound for the west, like the fox that turns homeward to die—he only wanted to see his native hills once more.
proposals.after: My brother Xiang crossed northward from Shan bound for the west, like the fox that turns homeward to die—he only wanted to see his native hills once more.
proposals.reason: The directional 北 modifies the crossing; it does not identify a starting place south of Shan.

proposals.before: Dou Chong led the van toward Chang'an from Fanchuan.
proposals.after: Fu Deng sent Dou Chong ahead with the troops at hand, then himself marched from Fanchuan toward Chang'an.
proposals.reason: The current field omits Fu Deng's action and collapses the dispatch of Dou Chong and Deng's own advance into one event.

proposals.before: Yao Chang's Wang Polu raided Qinzhou until Yang Ding shattered him at Genu Ford on the Qingshui.
proposals.after: Yao Chang's Wang Polu raided Qinzhou until Yang Ding shattered him at Genu Slope by Qingshui.
proposals.reason: 阪 is a slope, not a ford.

proposals.before: Hearing this, Fu Deng fattened the horses and told Fu Jian's tablet, "For twelve years I have borne your spear; heaven has blessed every blow and ice has cracked Yao Chang's ranks.
proposals.after: Hearing this, Fu Deng fattened the horses and told Fu Jian's tablet, "For nearly twelve years I have borne your spear; heaven has blessed every blow and ice has cracked Yao Chang's ranks.
proposals.reason: 幾將一紀 says the period was nearly one twelve-year cycle; the current field turns the approximation into an exact duration.

proposals.before: Deng contended for water and could not obtain it; of the host, twelve or thirteen parts died of thirst.
proposals.after: Deng contended for water and could not obtain it; two or three tenths of the host died of thirst.
proposals.reason: 十二三 is 十之二三, two or three tenths, not twelve or thirteen parts.

proposals.before: Fu Deng could not win the water; two men in three died of thirst.
proposals.after: Fu Deng could not win the water; two or three men in ten died of thirst.
proposals.reason: 十二三 denotes roughly twenty to thirty percent; 'two men in three' greatly overstates the deaths.

proposals.before: Fu Jian the heir widened that dark legacy, marched homesick veterans through the mountain gap, seized the sheer heights of the three Qin, dared covet the throne, and stole a king's title—among scheming strongmen he counts for something.
proposals.after: Fu Jian the heir widened that dark legacy, marched homesick veterans through the mountain gap, seized the sheer heights of the three Qin, dared covet the throne, ennobled men of talent from Chu, and built lodgings for those expected to submit.
proposals.reason: The current field omits 疏爵以侯楚材，築館以須歸命 and therefore drops two complete actions from the source.

proposals.before: Sparing the lives of the people, he suspected the morning hunger of fierce beasts.
proposals.after: He was ruthless with the lives of the people, as though fearing that fierce beasts would go hungry in the morning.
proposals.reason: In this condemnation of Fu Sheng's cruelty, 忍 means hard-hearted or ruthless; the current 'sparing' reverses the sense and conflicts with the surrounding account of mutilating punishments.

proposals.before: He spared the people yet suspected them like hungry beasts at dawn.
proposals.after: He slaughtered his people as if afraid that fierce beasts might miss their morning meal.
proposals.reason: The current wording reverses 忍 and makes the image's people and beasts exchange roles.

decisions.reason: 以子胤為鷹揚將軍 then 率眾五萬 assigns the fifty thousand to Yin, not Liang Xi (熙). Literal before wrongly makes Xi lead the host.
